lifetime_fix.summary: execute_completion now sweeps a call-local Heap exactly once on every exit from run(), rooting only Completion.value. The top-level execution environment is not a root, so environment<->declared-function cycles are reclaimed on success and failure paths alike. Caller-supplied heaps are never swept at exit; the caller owns all roots and collection, so runtime embedding behaviour is unchanged.

notes: Discovery evidence for the pre-fix standalone VM leak is retained as docs/evidence/memory-safety/post-preview-pc0v-vm-valgrind-fail.json plus the raw full log; the leak is not rewritten into a pass.
Post-fix Valgrind pass evidence is recorded per workload under docs/evidence/memory-safety/ with -pass suffixes at commit 15df113.

Contract boundary: a heap-backed completion value returned from local-heap execution is transferred as an owning shared_ptr and remains valid when its reachable value graph is acyclic; a self-referential returned graph (a closure capturing an environment that references it back) requires a caller-owned Heap. This is documented, not silently weakened.
PC0V is complete only at the tested JS++ commit 15df113 and TSCC commit 1bc3047; PC0P second-platform packaging remains pending.
